question: Russia x Ukraine ceasefire agreement by March 31, 2027?
requirements: This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is a ceasefire agreement between Russia and Ukraine by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.
context: Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A ceasefire agreement refers to any mutually-agreed suspension of direct military engagement between Russia and Ukraine, which is either officially announced by both countries or confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting to have been mutually agreed by both countries.

A broader peace deal, normalization agreement, political framework, truce, or humanitarian pause will qualify if it includes a mutually agreed suspension of direct military engagement, to be effective on a specified date.
Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures without an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not qualify.
Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation without an announced agreement, or unilateral pause in hostilities will not be considered a ceasefire agreement.
Only agreements which constitute a general pause in the conflict will qualify.
Agreements which only apply to specific conflict categories (e.g.
restrictions on certain target categories or certain locations) will not qualify.

If a qualifying agreement is officially reached before this market’s end date, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of whether the ceasefire agreement officially takes effect after that date.
The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of Russia and Ukraine and a consensus of credible reporting.

precedents: Geneva Sep 22 2026: NO agreement on fundamentals (territory, Zaporizhzhia); monitoring mechanism ~agreed; more talks unspecified (Moscow Times).
May 2026 3-day Victory-Day ceasefire: announced by Trump, immediately violated by both sides (1000+ claimed violations, PBS). Agreement != compliance.
Energy ceasefire Sep 2026: Ukraine ready, Russia non-committal; Trump claims vs reality gap (RBC/Euronews). Sectoral deals may not satisfy general wording.
Minsk I/II: 1289 violations in 9mo (OSCE 2020-21); Budapest 1994 broken 2014. Announced-then-violated is the base pattern.
US pushing sectoral path (energy, hospitals) per Amb. Whitaker Sep 17 — partial deals fragment the trigger.
alpha.crux: Market asks about AGREEMENT, not compliance — announced-but-violated counts if real. Thin text (one requirement, zero exclusions) means partial/sectoral deals sit in a gray zone. Near-term legs need a full agreement within weeks; talks produce monitoring mechanisms, not signatures.
alpha.misreading: Title readers price compliance (will fighting stop); conditions price announcement (was something agreed). May-2026 pattern shows announcements happen and fail — title direction right, payoff wrong without the distinction.
